Mr Shopper

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
You can buy anything from refrigerators, to electronics to gardening tools. But once they have your money, your order NEVER arrives.

Unique Selling Point:
MrShopper.co.za is a scam. It's pretends to be an online superstore like Makro selling everything, but actually its just a scam. You purchase the item you choose and it never arrives. They give you excuses but eventually just stop replying. We have over 50 submission which say this - NOT one customer getting their purchase: (ive combined them with this google doc). There are 1500 people in the facebook group dedicated to them as a scam, and hundreds of complaints on hellopeter. So why do they continue? They began last year during covid it popped up for every holiday, like fathers day, black friday etc claiming to have deals of less than 60%... Then they returned for Christmas. But so far nothing has been done because its quite hard to track online fraudsters. But now with the help of researcher Erin Klazar and an online investigator - they managed to track the fraudsters - two men whose names, photos and addresses we now have.

https://twitter.com/mrshoppersa

Please see the investigative report on Mr shopper



Summary:
The SA consumer commission haven't been able to do anything because they don't have the special expertise in order to track people through the internet, but they are experiencing a high number of these scams. They look real, and the consumer doesn't know it's a scam until their order never arrives.

Erin and her investigator are compiling a report for us right now, but we can go through the process with them and actually show how its done. There are various software programs used and you need lots of data - like email addresses and IP addresses. Either way, nothing they've done is illegal. But it will help us locate and track down these fraudsters and hopefully confront them - maybe with some angry customers with us.

Further information:
we have many case studies to choose from - so we can go through the list and decide...but they're all identical

From my own research: its used to be dialashopper in 2017 claiming to bring groceries, but then during covid last year the site changed and became MrShopper.co.za.

Press Release:


Elusive Online Scammer Busted

Online scams are easy to perpetuate – anyone, including scamsters, can create a website and hide behind privacy laws. But Carte Blanche was up for the challenge to find them after thousands of people, apparently scammed by an online retailer claiming to sell anything from dishwashers to baby products to bricks and swimming pools, complained to the show. After parting with their money, clients never saw their deliveries or refunds. Using online digital footprinting and good old-fashioned footwork to track down a group of young scammers in Pretoria and the Eastern Cape, we unravel the complicated connections.

Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein | Researcher: Erin Hommes | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:



Online shopping in the time Covid-19 is the perfect solution to avoiding the shops and staying safe, but still allows a shopper to attack Black Friday or Christmas sales. 

BUT WHAT IF THE STORE YOU CHOOSE ENDS UP NEVER SENDING YOU WHAT YOU ORDERED? WELL THAT'S EXACTLY WHAT THOUSANDS OF SHOPPERS SAY HAPPENED WITH MR SHOPPER ...Complaint video clips...

Launched in May 2020, everything seemed legitimate with slick advertising campaigns to compete with other online retailers.

P: I was looking for something and all the the usual big retailers had stock. I had didn't have stock. So I looked on Google and found Mr. Shopper and the pricing seemed reasonable. 

As an IT professional, Peter Wallace, thought he’d be immune to such scams, but he became frustrated when his delivery didn’t arrive.

P: We bought on the 29th of December and they promised delivery on, it was a Sunday, and my wife still remarked that how come they deliver this on a Sunday? Sunday came and went and nothing happened. So I sent an email and got a whole lot of excuses. So I said, you know what, just rather do a refund. About a month went by and I realized that here was a serious problem.

Carte Blanche has received almost 100 complaints about Mr Shopper… with 1000 more online... even a “Mr shopper South Africa Official Hate Page Group” on Facebook. Complaint video clips

Peter is compiling a list of angry customers.

P: I have an average spend of R4000 pp, we’re talking about a possible R24 million we are talking about it and that’s just the invoices we know about.

Wallace went all out: He complained to the online payment platform Payfast and the company said it ceased processing payments in December 2020. The hosting internet service provider Afrihost took the site down a week after Wallace's complaint, and it said it could only provide information to law enforcement. So we have informed the South African Police Service, and have been told that it intends combining all the cases.

SOUTH AFRICA IS ONE OF THE ONLY COUNTRIES IN THE WORLD THAT ACTUALLY TAKES DOWN WEBSITES, HOWEVER, THE BANKS, THE PAYMENT COMPANIES AND THE WEBSITE HOSTING SERVICES CANNOT DIVULGE AN ALLEGED SCAMMERS DETAILS OUT TO ANGRY CONSUMERS AND IT MAY BE THAT EXACT LAW THAT THESE SCAMMERS ARE RELYING ON TO GET AWAY WITH IT. BECAUSE WHILE THE WEBSITE MAY BE TAKEN DOWN YOU'LL NEVER KNOW WHO THEY ARE.

Acting Commissioner Joseph Selolo says The National Consumer Commission’s investigation has just begun.

Solelo: Jointly with the Consumer Goods Services Ombudsman, we have recently received in excess of 150 complaints and we are investigating to determine if there is any contravention of the Consumer Protection Act. Consumers can then approach their own banks and the banking ombuds for assistance. if we find there was prohibited conduct, we refer the matter to the tribunal. We prosecute the persons involved. Andrequest that consumers be refunded.

M: Hosting sites like Afrihost, which hosts such websites that have scammed people, what responsibility do they have to take these sites down?

Solelo: They do not necessarily vet the information. However, it would be of great assistance if such entities would then adopt a stance that says we don't want to taint ourselves. Let's do a little bit of research.

M: Are these scammers sitting in a small room and one does an online shopping scam and this and the other, how does it work?

Solelo: It's fairly easy what you've seen to create the website. Look, but the first thing is to identify the people behind these scams. And that's really, really, really difficult.

So how difficult is it to track down an alleged scamster? We asked Mybroadband’s Investigative Journalist Jan Vermeulen. 

They use at least fake identities and sometimes stolen identities so that when the authorities come after them, they chase their tails. And that's how they get away with it.

But we were up for that challenge… First, we found a company called Mr Shopper CC, but it was dead end as it had been deregistered in 2011. Next we went to their Midrand offices and a guard there gave us our first clues, saying some of them were foreign nationals even naming those in charge...

G: “These are younger guys, roughly 25, 23… Eddie and Brendon, two names.” 

THE GUARD HAS SAID THAT THESE GUYS HAVE ‘DONE A RUNNER’ AND DISAPPEARED. BUT WE REALLY WANTED TO KNOW WHO IS BEHIND MR SHOPPER, SO CARTE BLANCHE DECIDED TO SEEK THE RESEARCH HELP OF THOSE WHO CAN CRAWL THROUGH THE COMPLICATED INTERWEB AND TRACK THE SCAMMERS DOWN THROUGH THEIR DIGITAL FOOTPRINT.

We reached out to “Trinity” and her team, who have experience tracing individuals online.

A lot of effort was put into creating not just a website, but an identity around Mr. Shopper. They created social media sites, a website, they created positive reviews online. What we've done to track these people involved in Mr. Shopper in this sense is passive digital footprinting that we conducted; who was involved with the domain, what email addresses were linked. We have a look at whose cell phone numbers were associated with specific social media accounts, and so we start to build a profile of all the indiv involved.

Trinity identified this stock footage used to sell their website and products.

M: So they planted the Shopper logo on the sides? T: Yeah, and made these videos.

Masa: Fast and reliable delivery.Trinity: Not really.

Through this tracing exercise we followed several leads and identified the following characters  “Eddie”, Brendon Shaka, Lebogang amoga, Brian Mawela and Sean Khumbula, and another woman named Letisha Muzwazwa who was linked to the company's whatsapp number. 

T: We came across an interesting advert using exactly the same telephone number Advertising, all you need for tonight, just call and I will….

M: Come to you for what? T: I suppose you could use your imagination.

In a lucky break… the domain registration information was also leaked to our tracers, identifying the new owner as South African Anelisa Ncamisa...We went to her registered address… but no one knew her… so we called her. 

M: We're doing a story about a website called Mr Shopper. You're aware of the website, Mr Shopper? A: Correct. 

M: And it's registered under your name? A: Yes

M: Anelisa. You know, we've received thousands of complaints people go onto your website, they purchase items, they pay for them and they never get delivered. So that's a scam. Anelisa: They do get delivered, but at times there’s some delays that happens and they do get explanations. But then some customers they don't want it, so they do get their refunds back.

M: It's not one or two people, as you're putting it, or some delays, because people have made orders as far as last year, October, November, and they haven't received the items. It sounds like a scam to me. A: No, it's not. It's not. The thing is, there are many people have other things, especially last year. So like everyone is actually getting what you call getting to assist everyone at the moment. I understand the knowing because you never got out of the plastic industry and but everyone is going to be getting assistance.

We also asked Anelisa who works for her…..

M: How many people? A: I have like about four people, yes… It’s a lot of pressure.

M: So do you own the company and the four people, all your employees? yes.

We set up an interview for the next day in Pretoria, but she didn’t pitch, so we tracked her to the Eastern Cape, catching her in the early morning - her story then completely changed.

Anelisa: “I don’t know anything about this, it might be a mistaken identity.”

WHAT WE NOTED WAS THAT THE PACKAGES WERE MEANT TO BE SENT USING A SHIPPING SERVICE CALLED PELICAN EXPRESS… BUT A GOOGLE SEARCH SHOWS THE COMPANY HAVE NO WEBSITE - WHAT MORE SUSPICIOUS IS WHEN IT CAME ABOUT 

What was unusual about Pelican Express as well, it was also a company, brand new single director registered in July 2020 when we thought it was a little odd that, again, this courier company being used by Mr. Shopper was registered around the same time that Mr. Shopper started trading.

So we called the owner, Aviwe Ngcingwana who lives in this complex in Pretoria...

Sasha: Are you the owner of Pelican Express? A: yes

S: You're implicated in this? A: No

Did you deliver for MrShopper? A: Yes

Did you know it was a scam? A: No. We are still operating.

You guys have no website, i've never heard of you?” A: Can i call you some other time? haha

Did you speak to Brendon or eddie? A: Not yet. But I need to call some of them and find out what’s going on.

She never called back and never gave up the numbers -  It seemed Eddie was the missing piece to this puzzle.  Trinity dug deeper, and located a man named Edwin - a web developer who retweeted several mrshopper tweets. 

Eddie: “I have no idea what you’re talking about, you can call the police that’s what you can do. ”

Despite Anelisa and Edwin being facebook friends they both bizarrely claimed they don’t know each other.  Eddie: ”no” Anelisa…I don’t know eddie…” 

And despite his denials his photo was positively identified by a guard as the man who worked at the MrShopper headquarters…

Guard: “That’s him… they drove nice cars, those new latest ford rangers.”

MrShopper and its other employees were called and emailed but never responded to multiple requests. However, online Mrshopper says their bank account has been suspended for suspected fraudulent activity and they’re sourcing further capital.

Jan: These scams are highly syndicated. It's almost like just a normal job. You go you go to work in the morning, you know, you get dressed smartly, you're going to work in the morning. And what you do for a living is you scam people.

We then drew up an organogram on what the mrshopper network looked like… … although it was hard to find those allegedly implicated, we’ve proved it’s not impossible, and hopefully MrShopper has been all shopped out.
